note: Four clear matches and one material miss. Successful holds: a buy-side investment management professional running both trading and operations across US and Asia market hours — the 'or equivalent' branch of the criterion. Income holds: he probed the price three times but then paid $6,000 in full on a credit card and declined financing on his own analysis. Good_to_great holds in his own words — 'I feel like I'm on the right path, but now I feel like I hit that plateau and I'm ready to be on the next level' — and he has already done eighteen months of the work himself, from 220 lb to 190 lb. Not_deconditioned holds comfortably: he trains five to six times a week and does cardio classes on top, and is the opposite of gym-averse. The miss is neglected_health, and it is not close. The criterion wants health to be the deprioritised area rather than the emergency, and this is a man with a recurring lumbar sciatica cycle that disables him for roughly a month every four to five months, cervical symptoms radiating down his left arm, and a chiropractor as his only clinical relationship. He needed a folding cane in Barcelona and spent part of a Hawaii holiday confined to a hotel room. That is an active clinical problem with a good income attached, not neglect. This is now the fourth commercially-strong, clinically-complicated buyer in this batch, alongside Steve Dawson, Joseph and to a lesser extent Chris Wiley. The observation already recorded in icp.json — that the stated ICP has no clinical criterion — is no longer an occasional edge case in this corpus; on this rep's calls it is the modal profile of a closed deal. There is a second-order finding here too: the clinical condition was used commercially, as the stated reason the prospect should take the more expensive Trevor tier rather than the cheaper junior-coach tier.
